title: Cech cup resolution representatives
statement: Let U be an arbitrary open cover of a scheme X and F,G quasi-coherent modules. Fix canonical comparisons cF,cG,cFG [def-sc-module-cech-comparison] in degrees p,q,p+q. For Cech kernel cocycles a,b,c with underlying cochain c equal to the Alexander-Whitney product of a and b [def-sc-cech-cup-product], there exist a computing acyclic resolution pairing D [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data] and global kernel cocycles a',b',c' such that their D-class maps equal cF([a]),cG([b]),cFG([c]), respectively, and the underlying section of c' is D.pair(p,q,top)(a',b'). This concerns resolution representatives and assumes no cup product on cohomology.

proof.text: Obtain a computing resolution pairing D and Cech comparison data CL, CR, CT from lem-sc-cech-cup-resolution-comparison-exists. The class map of each acyclic resolution is surjective: its injective comparison induces a homology isomorphism, the injective-resolution identification is an isomorphism, and cycles surject onto homology. Lift cF([a]) and cG([b]) to global kernel cocycles a′,b′. The Leibniz equation and bilinearity of D.pair show that its value on these cocycles is a kernel cocycle c′.

Apply lem-sc-cech-cup-signed-axis-pairing to the six chain maps of CL,CR,CT and their six component equations. This gives one bilinear operation on total homology satisfying both alpha and beta axis formulas. CL.alpha_class and CL.beta_class, together with the chosen class of a′, identify H(alpha)([a′]) with H(beta)([a]); do the same for b′.

Evaluate the same total homology operation on the two pairs of equal classes. Its alpha formula gives H(alpha_target)([c′]); its beta formula and the hypothesis c=cechCupCochain(a,b) give H(beta_target)([c]). Compose this equality with CT.alpha_class and CT.beta_class and cancel the injective map CT.iso.hom. This yields D.target.class(c′)=cFG([c]). Return D,a′,b′,c′ with the chosen input-class equalities and the defining section equality.

theorem cechCup_resolution_representatives (X : Scheme.{v}) {ι : Type v}
    (U : ι → X.Opens) (hU : iSup U = ⊤)
    (F G : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] (p q : ℕ)
    (cF : ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat).homology p ⟶
      (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).obj F)
    (hcF : IsModuleCechComparison U F p cF)
    (cG : ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj G.presheafModuleCat).homology q ⟶
      (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace q).obj G)
    (hcG : IsModuleCechComparison U G q cG)
    (cFG : ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj (F ⊗ G).presheafModuleCat).homology (p + q) ⟶
      (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace (p + q)).obj (@id X.Modules (F ⊗ G)))
    (hcFG : IsModuleCechComparison U (F ⊗ G) (p + q) cFG)
    (a : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (b : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj G.presheafModuleCat).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (c : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj (F ⊗ G).presheafModuleCat).sc
      (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (hc : c.val = cechCupCochain U F G p q a.val b.val) :
    ∃ (D : CupResolutionPairing F G)
      (a' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
      (b' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
      (c' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
      D.left.class p a' = cF (cupCycleClass _ p a) ∧
      D.right.class q b' = cG (cupCycleClass _ q b) ∧
      D.target.class (p + q) c' = cFG (cupCycleClass _ (p + q) c) ∧
      c'.val = D.pair p q ⊤ a'.val b'.val
